title: Note colours and the Current colour
lede: Six toolbar swatches either recolour the Note being edited, or with none being edited, set the **Current colour** for the next Note. One command, `pickColour`, holds that rule. A colour is a `data-colour` attribute: global CSS maps it to three variables (background, strip, Editing strip), so a Note, a swatch and a New-button glyph all recolour by changing one attribute.

files.question: What does a swatch press do to the stores?
files.summary: `pickColour` recolours the edited Note through `recolour`, which also sets the Current colour. With nothing being edited, it sets only the Current colour.
files.owns: The rule that spans the Notes store and the UI store.
files.never: Touches the DOM or knows about swatches as buttons.

files.question: How does a recolour re-render only one Note?
files.summary: `setColour` replaces just that Note through `withNote`, so `ids` and every other Note keep their reference. Recolouring a missing Note, or with the same colour, returns the same state.
files.tested: Node tests in `notesReducer.test.ts`; a Profiler test in `colours.browser.test.tsx`.

files.question: Where does the Current colour live?
files.summary: `setCurrentColour` sets `currentColour`, which `createNote` already read. A no-op keeps the state.

files.question: How does a swatch keep the edited Note's focus and caret?
files.summary: Six buttons and a "this note / next note" label. A mouse press is prevented at `mousedown`, so focus never leaves the textarea; the click then calls `pickColour`.
files.owns: The swatches, which one is pressed, and the label.
files.never: Decides what a pick changes: that is `pickColour`.

files.question: Where does a Note get its colour?
files.summary: It already rendered `data-colour={colour}`; this PR only adds `data-grip-strip` to the strip, for the browser test.

files.question: Which variables does a Note read?
files.summary: `--note-bg`, `--note-strip`, and `--note-strip-editing` while Editing. The yellow-only `data-colour` rule moved to `tokens.css`.
files.tested: Browser test of the three shades per colour.

files.question: How does one attribute give three shades?
files.summary: Eighteen colour tokens, and one `[data-colour='…']` rule per colour that maps them to `--note-bg`, `--note-strip` and `--note-strip-editing`.
files.owns: The palette, each background above 12:1 against `--color-note-text`.
files.never: Styles a component: each component reads the three variables.
files.tested: A browser test that every colour gives three distinct, non-transparent shades.

files.question: How do the New buttons show the Current colour?
files.summary: They subscribe to `currentColour` and put it on a glyph's `data-colour`.
files.never: Re-renders as Notes change: Notes are still read at press time.

steps.title: mousedown on the Pink swatch
steps.explain: Focus moves as the default action of `mousedown`, so preventing it there keeps focus, and with it the selection, in the textarea. Preventing `pointerdown` alone would not be enough here. Nothing ends Editing either: only a press on empty Board or on another Note does. The browser test sets the caret at 3 and finds it still at 3 after the press, in Chromium and Firefox.

steps.title: click: the Note turns pink, and so does the Current colour
steps.explain: `pickColour` reads `editingId` at click time and hands the edited Note to `recolour`. That checks the Note exists before touching either store, so a stale id can't change the Current colour on its own. `setColour` replaces only that Note, which is why the Profiler test sees Note a re-render and not Note b.

steps.title: render: one attribute, three shades
steps.explain: The Note already renders `data-colour={colour}`, and the global rule for `pink` swaps the three variables. The Grip strip reads `--note-strip-editing` while the Note is being edited, so each colour has its own Editing shade rather than a computed `color-mix`.

steps.title: render: the swatches show this Note's colour
steps.explain: While Editing, the pressed swatch is the edited Note's colour, not the Current colour. Both are the same right after a pick, but they differ when you start editing an older Note. The selector returns a primitive, so the swatches re-render only when that colour changes, not on every keystroke.

steps.explain: `createNote` was already reading the Current colour; this PR gives the user a way to change it.

notes.title: The pressed swatch follows the edited Note, not the Current colour
notes.detail: The issue doesn't say which swatch looks pressed. Showing the edited Note's colour answers "what colour is this note?", which matches the "this note" label. The counter-argument: right after you start editing an older Note, the New-button glyphs (Current colour) and the pressed swatch can disagree. They agree again after the first pick.

notes.title: Keyboard users move focus to the swatch
notes.detail: Only a mouse press keeps focus in the Note. Tabbing to a swatch takes focus off the textarea, but Editing doesn't end on blur, so Enter or Space still recolours the edited Note. Focus is not sent back to the textarea; doing that would make the swatches impossible to step through with Tab.

notes.title: Colour rules moved to global CSS
notes.detail: The `[data-colour]` rules left `Note.module.css` for `tokens.css`, so swatches and glyphs reuse them. A seventh colour means editing `NOTE_COLOURS`, `COLOUR_NAMES` and `tokens.css`; plain CSS has no loop to avoid the six repeated rules.

notes.title: Strips are below 12:1
notes.detail: The 12:1 rule holds for the backgrounds, which carry the text (lowest: orange, 12.09). Strip shades go down to about 8:1 on the Editing strips. They hold only the ×, which is drawn at reduced opacity anyway.

notes.title: The Current colour isn't saved
notes.detail: Like the Notes themselves, it is lost on reload until the local copy (#9) lands.
